The FIR was filed under various sections of the Indian Penal Code, including 304 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) and 337 (causing hurt by endangering life or personal safety of others). The court found that the college had organized the trip with necessary permissions and that the students had not followed safety protocols. The ruling emphasized that the educational institution cannot be held liable for the students' actions during the trip. The principal and teachers expressed relief at the verdict, highlighting the importance of clear guidelines for school excursions. legal.summary: The Delhi High Court dismissed a petition challenging the framing of charges against a woman in a gang rape case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. The court ruled that the term 'persons' in Section 376-D of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Section 70 of the POCSO Act is gender neutral. This means that a woman can be charged if she acts in furtherance of a common intention to commit rape. The case highlights the court's interpretation of gender roles in criminal culpability, emphasizing that all individuals, regardless of gender, can be implicated in such serious offenses when they share a common intent.
